content.title: About
content.content: Cooked fish (e.g., boiled, baked, fried) is used as an ingredient in a wide variety of dishes. Cooking retains most nutrients, softens the flesh, and imparts a distinctive flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cooked fish is a common component of soups, stews, salads, and pasta dishes.
Different cooking methods (steaming, baking, frying) affect fat content and aromatic compounds.
Fish has been one of the earliest sources of protein in human diets.
Cooking reduces parasites and bacteria, making the product safer.
In some cultures, cooked fish is served cold as appetizers or in sushi.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Cooked fish provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Most fish retain EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12, B6, and niacin aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Fish supplies iodine, selenium, phosphorus, and iron, important for thyroid function, antioxidant protection, and bone health.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many meat products, fish generally contains less saturated fat, making it suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to fish and seafood.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Certain species (e.g., shark, swordfish) can accumulate mercury; consumption should be limited.

items.title: Undercooking hazards
items.content: Insufficiently cooked fish may contain harmful bacteria and parasites.

items.title: High sodium in processed dishes
items.content: Prepared fish seasoned with salt or sauces can be high in sodium, which is undesirable for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked fish can be added to salads, pastas, rice or potato dishes, used as fillings for pies and rolls, or served as a standalone main course with side vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked fish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze it for 1‑2 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or slimy texture.
